rv.q: I found it playful, thoughtful, and deliciously up-to-the-minute.
Hussain’s splatter gun approach to obvious societal evils makes some intriguing points but misses more than it hits, especially in the early parts of Word-Play.
These scenes are a bit of a hotchpotch, some more memorable than others.

cn.t: Critics offer mixed-to-positive reviews, praising Rabiah Hussain's sharp political satire and incisive exploration of language and power, though some find the Downing Street premise more effective in concept than execution.
